clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy presented with worsening headache, fever, increased frontal swelling, and pain behind the right eye, following an initial course of penicillin for similar symptoms. Imaging studies, including CT and MRI, revealed signs of bone erosions in the frontal sinuses, frontal bone osteomyelitis, slight maxillary, ethmoidal, and frontal sinusitis, as well as epidural and periosteal abscesses in communication with the osteomyelitis. MRI also showed partial obstruction of the superior sagittal sinus due to reactive phlebitis. Blood cultures yielded Streptococcus anginosus. Despite the presence of abscesses, neurosurgery determined no indication for surgical intervention due to the absence of neurological deficits and the patient's well-being. The patient was treated with a six-week course of intravenous antibiotics.

MRI revealed partial obstruction in the anterior third part of the superior sagittal sinus due to reactive phlebitis without thrombosis.
Subsequent CT scan of the cerebrum gave a full visualization of the frontal bone erosion internally on the right side.
Cultures of blood yielded Streptococcus anginosus.
Neurosurgery department found no indication for surgical intervention due to no neurological deficits and the patient’s well-being.
Patient continued intravenous antibiotic treatment for six weeks in total.
